en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Miqdad, who said: I and two companions of mine arrived having lost our hearing and our sight due to exhaustion and hunger. We began presenting ourselves to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), but not one of them could take us in. So we came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he took us to his family, and behold, there were three goats. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Milk this milk among us." He said: So we used to milk them, and each person among us would drink his share, and we would set aside for the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) his share. He said: And he would come at night and offer greetings in such a way that would not wake a sleeping person and yet could be heard by one who was awake. He said: Then he would come to the mosque and pray, then come to his drink and drink it. One night, Satan came to me after I had already drunk my share and said: "Muhammad visits the Ansar and they gift him delicacies, and he finds among them whatever he needs without needing this draught!" So I went to it and drank it. But when it had entered my stomach and I knew there was no way to retrieve it—he said—Satan made me feel regret, saying: "Woe to you! What have you done? Have you drunk the drink of Muhammad? Now he will come and not find it, and he will supplicate against you, so you will perish and your worldly life and your Hereafter will be ruined!" And I had a woolen wrapper (shamlah); whenever I placed it over my feet, my head remained uncovered, and whenever I placed it over my head, my feet remained uncovered, and sleep would not come to me, while my two companions slept, having not done what I had done. He said: Then the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came and offered greetings just as he used to offer greetings, then came to the mosque and prayed, then came to his drink and uncovered it, but found nothing in it. He raised his head toward the heaven, so I said to myself: "Now he will supplicate against me and I will perish!" But he said: "O Allah, feed him who has fed me, and give drink to him who has given me drink." He said: So I took hold of the woolen wrapper, fastened it around myself, grabbed the blade, and went to the goats to see which of them was fattest so that I might slaughter it for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). And behold, its udder was full of milk—nay, all of them were full of milk! So I went to a vessel belonging to the household of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that they never hoped to milk into—he said—and I milked into it until foam rose to its brim. Then I brought it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said: "Have you drunk your drink tonight?" He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, drink!" So he drank, then handed it to me. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, drink!" So he drank, then handed it to me. When I knew that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had quenched his thirst and that I had attained his supplication, I laughed until I fell to the ground. He said: Thereupon the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "One of your misdeeds, O Miqdad!" So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, my situation was such-and-such, and I did such-and-such." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "This is nothing but a mercy from Allah; could you not have informed me so that we might wake our two companions and they could partake of it?" He said: I said: "By the One Who sent you with the truth, I do not care—now that you have received it and I have received it with you—who among people receives it!"
